issues.body:
This PR converts the `[GPT-5.6]` header marker to `[SPARQ agent]` in eight files spanning REG-1 through REG-5 (policy/repos.toml, the three workflows, dispatch-claim.py, groom.py, policy-resolve.py, worker-issue.py, worker-prep.sh). A tree-wide search finds exactly one instance left:

  containers/worker-model.Dockerfile:1: # [GPT-5.6] REG-3 model sandbox: pinned Node runtime for the routed CLIs plus the target's Rust

That file is in the same REG-numbered series as the converted set (its own header says "REG-3", the same phase as worker-issue.py and worker-prep.sh), so there is no visible principle by which it would be out of scope. Leaving it means the repo still contains a hard-coded model marker after a change whose entire purpose is to remove them, and the next reader has no way to tell whether the survivor is an oversight or a deliberate exception.

This is not a correctness or trust-plane defect — nothing reads the string — but the review bar here is correct AND complete, and 8/9 is not complete.

I am attaching this to policy/repos.toml because the schema requires a path from the diff; the file needing the edit is containers/worker-model.Dockerfile.

(Scope caveat: I could not read issue #1621. If the maintainer deliberately excluded containers/, say so in the PR body and this drops to a nit.)
issues.fix_hint: Change containers/worker-model.Dockerfile line 1 from `# [GPT-5.6] REG-3 model sandbox: ...` to `# [SPARQ agent] REG-3 model sandbox: ...`, matching the other eight. Afterwards `grep -rn '\[GPT-5\.6\]' . ` (excluding .git) should return nothing. Leave the PROSE mentions of GPT-5.6 alone — README.md:84/250/262, orchestration/routing.toml:254/268, policy/repos.toml:5/10/16/23, scripts/triage.py:186 and the worker-live.sh display-name table are factual model-naming taxonomy (issue #97 requires the variant-qualified names), not authorship markers, and must not be genericized.
issues.title: Incomplete sweep: containers/worker-model.Dockerfile:1 still carries the `[GPT-5.6]` marker this PR removes everywhere else

issues.body:
The bracketed `[SPARQ agent]` header form did not exist anywhere in the repo before this diff. The convention the agent definitions actually document (.claude/agents/registry-*.md, "Provenance & identity") is the blockquote self-ID `> 🤖 SPARQ agent` for PR bodies and design records, plus a prohibition on hard-coding model markers; it says nothing about a source-file header bracket.

Meanwhile 43 files still carry `[OPUS-5]`, `[FABLE-5]`, `[HAIKU-...]` or `[GPT-5.6]` headers, four of them touched by this very diff:
  - scripts/policy-resolve.py: `[SPARQ agent]` (line 2) alongside `[OPUS-5]` (43, 63, 120) and `[FABLE-5]` (116)
  - policy/repos.toml: `[SPARQ agent]` (line 1) alongside `[FABLE-5]` (14, 21)

So within a single file the bracket now denotes an agent in one comment and a model in the next, with no written rule to tell them apart. That is a readability regression against the pre-change state, where the bracket consistently meant "the model that authored this".

Not a blocker: comments only, nothing parses them.
issues.fix_hint: Pick one and make it explicit. Either (a) land a one-paragraph rule in AGENTS.md defining `[SPARQ agent]` as the header provenance marker, stating that residual `[OPUS-5]`/`[FABLE-5]`/`[HAIKU-*]` markers are legacy and are converted on touch — which makes the mixed state a documented migration rather than drift; or (b) convert the remaining in-file markers in the eight files this PR already opens, so at least no single file mixes the two meanings. Option (a) is cheaper and keeps this diff small.
issues.title: New `[SPARQ agent]` bracket form is undocumented and now collides with surviving `[OPUS-5]`/`[FABLE-5]` markers in the same files

verdict.summary:
Comment-only diff: 9 header lines across 8 files (3 workflows, 4 scripts, policy/repos.toml) swap the hard-coded authorship marker `[GPT-5.6]` for the model-agnostic `[SPARQ agent]`. Direction is right and runtime risk is nil — every changed line is an inert comment (line 1 of the YAML/TOML files, line 2 of the .py/.sh files, ahead of the module docstring / `set -euo pipefail`), line counts are 1:1 so no byte-offset or line-anchored assertion shifts, and I found no code, self-test, classifier or fixture anywhere in the tree that greps for the literal `[GPT-5.6]` or for a `^# \[` header marker. No README/runbook copy of these header lines exists, so readme-runbook-check has nothing to diverge from. No self-test is required because no executable line is touched.

It is nonetheless INCOMPLETE, which is why this is request_changes rather than approve. `containers/worker-model.Dockerfile:1` still carries `# [GPT-5.6] REG-3 model sandbox: ...` — the last surviving instance of exactly the marker this PR exists to remove, on a file in the same REG-numbered trust-plane series as the eight that were converted. A sweep that leaves 1 of 9 behind does not achieve its stated end state and silently reads as "done".

Secondary: the diff introduces a bracketed `[SPARQ agent]` header form that exists nowhere else in the repo (the documented self-ID in .claude/agents/*.md is the blockquote `> 🤖 SPARQ agent`, for PR bodies and records), while 42 files — including four of the eight touched here — keep `[OPUS-5]`/`[FABLE-5]` markers. policy-resolve.py now reads `[SPARQ agent]` at line 2 and `[OPUS-5]` at line 43; policy/repos.toml reads `[SPARQ agent]` at line 1 and `[FABLE-5]` at lines 14 and 21. The bracket now means "agent" in some places and "model" in others, with no written rule to disambiguate.
